title: Build a custom area profile
meta_description: Create your own profile for local areas in England and Wales using Census 2021 data.
lede: Create your own profile for local areas with data for England and Wales.

body.text: Get data by different area types, for example your neighbourhood, ward or parish by using our tool to [build a custom area profile](https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/customprofiles).
search for an area by name or postcode
draw your own area using a polygon or circle on the map
choose different datasets for your area profile
save the area you have drawn to use again
save or print your area profile as an image, or embed it into a website using a code
[Tell us what you think](https://consultations.ons.gov.uk/digital-publishing/2ff010d4/consultation/intro/) about build a custom area profile content by answering a few questions.

body.title: Build a custom profile for your area

body.text: Build a custom area profile uses data from Nomis, an Office for National Statistics (ONS) service. Find all the data by [visiting the Nomis website](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/).

The data and boundaries displayed in these profiles are aggregated from small areas on a best-fit basis, and therefore may differ slightly from other sources. Values from Census 2021 datasets may vary slightly from other published statistics because the "cell-key method" adds a small amount of noise to some cells in published datasets to protect against disclosure by differencing. Our [Statistical Disclosure Control (SDC) for 2021 UK Census (Word, 257KB).](https://uksa.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/EAP125-Statistical-Disclosure-Control-SDC-for-2021-UK-Census.docx) report sets out the strategies used to lower the risk of disclosure.

You can get the geography data used in this tool, including [Output Area boundaries](https://www.ons.gov.uk/methodology/geography/ukgeographies/censusgeographies/census2021geographies) and lookup tables, on the [ONS Open Geography Portal](https://geoportal.statistics.gov.uk/).
